title: Formal differential adjoint and its principal symbol in every order
statement: All vector spaces are over $\mathbf R$ [def-weil-field]. Let $N$ be a Hausdorff second-countable oriented smooth manifold without boundary [def-sfb-smooth-real-manifold], of dimension $m\geq1$, with a smooth positive volume form $dV$ [def-sfb-oriented-smooth-volume]. Let $G,H$ be smooth real vector bundles of finite ranks [def-sfb-smooth-real-vector-bundle], equipped with smooth positive definite fibre metrics. Let $d\geq0$ be an integer and let $Q:\Gamma^\infty(G)\to\Gamma^\infty(H)$ be a real-linear differential operator with smooth coefficients of order at most $d$ [def-sfb-smooth-differential-operator], locally $Q=\sum_{|\alpha|\leq d}b_\alpha(x)\partial^\alpha$. There exists a unique real-linear differential operator $Q^*:\Gamma^\infty(H)\to\Gamma^\infty(G)$ with smooth coefficients of order at most $d$ such that $$\int_N\langle Qv,w\rangle_H\,dV=\int_N\langle v,Q^*w\rangle_G\,dV$$ whenever $v,w$ are smooth and at least one has compact support. Its degree-$d$ principal symbol is $$\sigma_d(Q^*)(x,\xi)=(-1)^d\sigma_d(Q)(x,\xi)^*,$$ where $\sigma_d(Q)(x,\xi)=\sum_{|\alpha|=d}b_\alpha(x)\xi^\alpha$ and the star on the right is the adjoint of a linear map for the fibre metrics. In local orthonormal frames it is the ordinary matrix transpose. Compactness of $N$ is not assumed.

source.place: WANTED locally; Demailly, Complex Analytic and Differential Geometry, June 21, 2012, VI §1, definition (1.5), local formula (1.6) and symbol formula (1.7), printed pp.288--289 (PDF pages 288--289), Euclidean-bundle case; read online https://www-fourier.univ-grenoble-alpes.fr/~demailly/manuscripts/agbook.pdf

proof.text:
In an oriented trivializing chart $U\subset\mathbf R^m$, write $dV=\rho\,dx$ with $\rho>0$, and let $M_G,M_H$ be the real positive definite Gram matrices in the chosen smooth frames. Put $C_\alpha=\rho b_\alpha^tM_H$ and define
$$R_Uw=(\rho M_G)^{-1}\sum_{|\alpha|\le d}(-1)^{|\alpha|}\partial^\alpha(C_\alpha w).$$
This is an explicit construction, not a choice from existence. The inverses are smooth: the adjugate formula expresses each entry of $M_G^{-1}$ as a polynomial in its entries times $(\det M_G)^{-1}$; its determinant never vanishes by positive definiteness. Apply [lem-sfb-smooth-nonzero-complex-reciprocal] to the real functions $\det M_G$ and $\rho$, viewed in $\mathbf C$; their reciprocals remain real. The product rule, iterated $|\alpha|$ times, expresses $R_U$ as a finite sum of derivatives of $w$ of orders at most $d$, with smooth real matrix coefficients. Thus $R_U$ is real-linear and differential of order at most $d$.

proof.text:
Specialize [lem-sfb-coordinate-weighted-adjoint] to scalar functions, identity Gram matrices, density $1$, $B=0$, and $A_j=1$ for one chosen coordinate and $A_k=0$ otherwise. Restrict its complex functions to real-valued functions. It gives $\int_U(\partial_j f)g\,dx=-\int_U f(\partial_jg)\,dx$ when at least one function has compact support in $U$. For a multi-index $\alpha$, repeat this identity $|\alpha|$ times, moving one derivative at a time. At each application the derivatives of the initially compact factor are still supported in its original compact support. The resulting identity is
$$\int_U(\partial^\alpha f)g\,dx=(-1)^{|\alpha|}\int_U f\partial^\alpha g\,dx.$$
Apply this to $f=v_a$ and $g=(C_\alpha w)_a$ and sum over $a,\alpha$. Since $\langle Qv,w\rangle_H\rho=\sum_{a,\alpha}(\partial^\alpha v_a)(C_\alpha w)_a$ and $\langle v,R_Uw\rangle_G\rho=v^t\sum_\alpha(-1)^{|\alpha|}\partial^\alpha(C_\alpha w)$, this proves the local adjunction identity for $R_U$. If $w$ is the compact factor, each $C_\alpha w$ is compactly supported; if $v$ is compact, each derivative of $v_a$ is. Thus either support hypothesis suffices.

proof.text: Prove uniqueness locally before gluing. Suppose $R,S$ are smooth differential operators satisfying the local identity for compactly supported tests. Fix compactly supported smooth $w$ and set $h=(R-S)w$. Taking $v=ge_a$ for a smooth real scalar test $g$ with compact support in $U$, subtraction gives $\int_U g\rho(M_Gh)_a\,dx=0$. Extend $f_a=\rho(M_Gh)_a$ by zero outside $U$. It is continuous on $U$, so [lem-sfb-continuous-local-integrability] gives the local integrability required by [lem-sfb-smooth-test-ae-separation]. That node applies to these real tests (viewing $f_a$ as complex-valued) and gives $f_a=0$ almost everywhere on $U$. By [lem-sfb-continuous-ae-pointwise], $f_a$ is identically zero on $U$. Invertibility of $\rho M_G$ gives $h=0$. No continuity of the zero extension at the boundary of $U$ was used.

proof.text: For any smooth local $w$ and $x\in U$, choose $0<a<b$ with $\overline B(x,b)\subset U$. By [lem-sfb-euclidean-smooth-bump] choose $\beta=1$ near $x$ with compact support $\overline B(x,b)$. Then $\beta w$, extended by zero, is a compactly supported smooth section, and step 3 gives $R(\beta w)=S(\beta w)$. Since differential operators depend only on the germ, $Rw(x)=Sw(x)$. This proves local uniqueness for unrestricted smooth inputs. The same cutoff extends any smooth germ to a global smooth section, a fact used below when passing between local and global operators.

proof.text:
On an overlap write $y=\phi(x)$, $v_x=P(x)v_y(\phi(x))$, and $w_x=T(x)w_y(\phi(x))$ for the smooth invertible frame matrices. Then $M_{G,y}\circ\phi=P^tM_{G,x}P$, $M_{H,y}\circ\phi=T^tM_{H,x}T$, and $(\rho_y\circ\phi)|\det d\phi|=\rho_x$. By [lem-sfb-euclidean-jacobian-integral] these identities preserve the two scalar pairing integrals under change of chart; the inputs have compact support, preserved by the diffeomorphism. Transfer the $x$-chart candidate to the $y$ chart by
$$\widetilde R_yw_y=\bigl(P^{-1}R_x(T(w_y\circ\phi))\bigr)\circ\phi^{-1}.$$
The repeated chain and product rules express a derivative of order $k$ of $T(w_y\circ\phi)$ using derivatives of $w_y$ of orders at most $k$; this follows by induction, since one further differentiation increases that order by at most one. Hence $\widetilde R_y$ is smooth and differential of order at most $d$. The transferred adjunction identity of step 2 says it is adjoint to the given $y$-chart expression of $Q$. Steps 3–4 now imply $\widetilde R_y=R_y$. Thus the local candidates agree as bundle-valued operators on every overlap.

proof.text: For a smooth section $w$ of $H$, define $Q^*w$ by $R_U(w|_U)$ in each trivializing chart. Step 5 says that these are the same vector in the fibre of $G$ on overlaps, so they define a unique global section, smooth because it is smooth in every chart. This assignment is real-linear and locally has the expression in step 1, hence is a differential operator with smooth coefficients of order at most $d$.

proof.text: Let $K$ be the compact support of whichever of $v,w$ is compactly supported. Choose finitely many trivializing charts $V_i$ covering $K$ and put $O=\bigcup_iV_i$. This open submanifold is Hausdorff and sigma-compact: every open subset of $\mathbf R^m$ is covered by its countable collection of closed rational balls contained in it. Thus [lem-sfb-smooth-subordinate-partition] applies on $O$ to the closed subset $K$ and the finite open cover $V_i$. Let $\varphi_i$ be its functions. If $v$ is compactly supported, set $v_i=\varphi_i v$ on $O$, extended by zero to $N$. Each $v_i$ is smooth, has compact support contained in $V_i$, and $\sum_i v_i=v$. Sum the local identities of step 2 for $v_i,w|_{V_i}$ to get the required global identity: linearity gives $\sum_iQv_i=Qv$, including all derivatives of the partition functions. If only $w$ is compactly supported, instead set $w_i=\varphi_i w$ and sum the identities for $v|_{V_i},w_i$; now $\sum_iQ^*w_i=Q^*w$. These are finite sums. All pairing integrals are genuine integrals: the local scalar pairing functions, extended by zero, are continuous with compact support, so [lem-sfb-continuous-compact-support-integrable] applies. Step 5 identifies these chart integrals with the volume-form integrals on $N$. Only $O$, not $N$, needed sigma-compactness.

proof.text:
Read the highest-order coefficients from step 1. Repeated Leibniz gives
$$\partial^\alpha(C_\alpha w)=\sum_{\gamma\le\alpha}\binom\alpha\gamma(\partial^{\alpha-\gamma}C_\alpha)\partial^\gamma w.$$
For $|\gamma|=d$, $|\alpha|\le d$ and $\gamma\le\alpha$ force $\gamma=\alpha$ and $|\alpha|=d$. Thus the degree-$d$ coefficient of $Q^*$ is $(-1)^d M_G^{-1}b_\alpha^tM_H$. The fibre adjoint of $b_\alpha$ is exactly $M_G^{-1}b_\alpha^tM_H$, since $\langle b_\alpha u,z\rangle_H=u^tb_\alpha^tM_Hz$. Multiplying by the real scalar $\xi^\alpha$ and summing gives the asserted symbol equality. In orthonormal frames both Gram matrices are the identity, so this is the ordinary transpose. This calculation uses precisely the symbol convention of the statement, with no factor of $i$.

proof.text: If another global differential operator satisfies the asserted adjunction, use compact tests supported in one chart and extend by zero to obtain its local adjunction. Steps 3–4 imply equality with the constructed operator on every local smooth germ, and hence globally. For $d=0$, step 1 reduces to $Q^*w=M_G^{-1}b_0^tM_Hw$, confirming the sign and the symbol formula. When $Q$ has order less than $d$, all degree-$d$ coefficients on both sides are zero by step 8. On a component where either bundle has rank zero, $Q$ and $Q^*$ are zero and all identities are interpreted as equalities of zero maps; the nonempty-matrix argument is needed only where both ranks are positive. On the empty manifold the assertions are vacuous. No completeness, finite volume, or compactness of $N$ was used.

Let $d\geq0$ be an integer and let $Q:\Gamma^\infty(G)\to\Gamma^\infty(H)$ be a real-linear differential operator with smooth coefficients of order at most $d$, locally $Q=\sum_{|\alpha|\leq d}b_\alpha(x)\partial^\alpha$. There exists a unique real-linear differential operator $Q^*:\Gamma^\infty(H)\to\Gamma^\infty(G)$ with smooth coefficients of order at most $d$ such that $$\int_N\langle Qv,w\rangle_H\,dV=\int_N\langle v,Q^*w\rangle_G\,dV$$ whenever $v,w$ are smooth and at least one has compact support. Its degree-$d$ principal symbol is $$\sigma_d(Q^*)(x,\xi)=(-1)^d\sigma_d(Q)(x,\xi)^*,$$ where $\sigma_d(Q)(x,\xi)=\sum_{|\alpha|=d}b_\alpha(x)\xi^\alpha$ and the star on the right is the adjoint of a linear map for the fibre metrics. In local orthonormal frames it is the ordinary matrix transpose. Compactness of $N$ is not assumed.
